headline: Ross Smith beats Schindler 11-8 to win the European Championship
standfirst: Ross Smith won the European Championship in Dortmund, beating Germany's Martin Schindler 11-8 and hitting 35 maximums.
body: Ross Smith won the 2026 European Championship at the Westfalenhalle in Dortmund, beating Martin Schindler 11-8 in the final. Smith averaged 92.92 and Schindler 91.49.

Smith's best performance came in the quarter-finals, where he averaged 107.00 to beat Luke Woodhouse 10-6. He also beat Karel Sedlacek 6-4 and Damon Heta 10-7, and then Gerwyn Price 11-7 in the semi-finals.

Schindler had a strong run on home soil. He averaged 103.16 to beat Jonny Clayton 10-1 in the quarter-finals, including a 167 checkout, the highest of the event. He then beat Krzysztof Ratajski 11-6 in the semi-finals.
Ratajski knocked out Luke Littler 10-6 in the quarter-finals. Littler had produced the best average of the tournament, 114.47, against Nathan Aspinall in the last 16.
Woodhouse hit a nine-dart finish in his first-round win over Dirk van Duijvenbode. Smith hit 35 maximums, well clear of Littler on 20.
Luke Humphries missed the event through illness and was replaced by Kim Huybrechts.
